item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] 'Give peace a chance': Israeli protesters urge opposition to ally with Arab parties
item.description:
'Give peace a chance': Israeli protesters urge opposition to ally with Arab parties

Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday's election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Netanyahu's hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.

Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20 percent of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.

"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, was a "great manipulator".

"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."

Tuesday's election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.

Jewish-majority parties opposed to Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.

An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.

Arab parties have only once formally sat in an Israeli government, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition that lasted from 2021 to 2022.

He has voiced a willingness to do so again.

Eisenkot, 66, a former military chief and political novice, largely shares Netanyahu's views on security issues including Gaza, which Israel has reduced to rubble since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023.

Eisenkot reiterated on Saturday that he would only form a "Zionist government" whose members commit to the "recognition of Israel as a Jewish, democratic and liberal state" and to the "recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation", conditions that Arab leaders have previously refused to accept.

While he has said he does not want a government dependent on Arab lists, Eisenkot has not explicitly rejected their external support.

"I want them (the opposition bloc) to go ahead to be brave and do the right thing," said demonstrator Sharon Balaban, 55, a video artist in Jerusalem. 

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Lebanese foreign minister urges Gulf states to help restore country's sovereignty
item.description:
Lebanese foreign minister urges Gulf states to help restore country's sovereignty

Lebanon's Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji has called for a complete Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territories, an end to ongoing attacks and the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, while urging Gulf states to support efforts to restore Lebanon's sovereignty.

Speaking at the 22nd Manama Dialogue, organised by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Rajji said restoring state authority was essential to Lebanon's stability and its relations with Arab countries, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.

He said Lebanon, under President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, had embarked on a path to reassert state control, pointing to government decisions aimed at placing all weapons under state authority and banning Hezbollah's military and security activities.

"Lebanon will no longer allow its territory to be used against the security of its Arab brothers or as a bargaining chip in negotiations conducted beyond its borders," Rajji said during a session on the Eastern Mediterranean.

The minister also reaffirmed Lebanon's solidarity with Bahrain and other Gulf states in "confronting Iranian attacks and those carried out by armed groups linked to Tehran", rejecting any violation of their sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.

He warned against allowing countries to "pursue regional ambitions through armed groups operating outside state authority", saying Lebanon had "experienced the devastating consequences of such organisations being used as instruments of foreign influence".

The Lebanese people, he said, had paid a heavy price for "wars they had never chosen to fight".

Rajji also raised concerns over maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, arguing that Gulf security could no longer be separated from developments in the Red Sea, which was closely linked to the security of the Eastern Mediterranean.

He called for a comprehensive Arab strategic partnership to address regional challenges, built around strong and sovereign states whose legitimate institutions retain exclusive authority over decisions of war and peace.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] MotoGP faces Qatar security concerns ahead of Grand Prix
item.description:
MotoGP faces Qatar security concerns ahead of Grand Prix

MotoGP is set to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix even as a group of riders demand more assurances for travelling to the region, with organisers arguing that a "zero-risk environment" is unrealistic.

The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to 6 November to 8 due to the US-Israeli war against Iran.

"MotoGP has provided teams and riders with every assurance available from the State of Qatar, the circuit ... and our own ongoing risk assessment processes," a MotoGP spokesperson said.

"We fully respect the concerns raised and highlight that safety remains the priority for everyone involved."

However, the MotoGP spokesperson said the expectation of a zero-risk environment was not realistic anywhere in the world by any government or organiser.

"Over the past months, we have maintained continuous dialogue with teams and riders, sharing the latest information available, providing direct access to documents and answering questions openly and transparently," the spokesperson said.

Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO of MotoGP, visited Qatar on Thursday, where the circuit's president, Abdulrahman Al-Mannai, said they were ready to welcome the riders, teams and fans for the 20th round of the season.

However, Spain's embassy in Qatar has issued a notice urging its citizens not to travel to the Gulf nation unless absolutely necessary.

Spaniards make up the largest share of riders on the grid, including world champion Marc Marquez.

Report by Reuters

A former Mossad agent who became a naturalised US citizen helped Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro leave the country in defiance of a judicial order barring him from travelling abroad, CNN Brasil has reported, citing findings from a Brazilian security agency investigation.

The former Israeli intelligence officer, whose identity has not been disclosed, arrived in Brazil on October 19, six days before the runoff, and accompanied Bolsonaro from Brasilia to the Argentine border.

Brazilian investigators traced two commercial vans crossing the Tancredo Neves Bridge, linking Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil with Puerto Iguazú in Argentina, using security camera footage. Bolsonaro and the former Mossad agent travelled in one vehicle, while his wife and two daughters were in the second. One driver was identified as a former municipal councillor from Foz do Iguaçu, while the other was his son.

After crossing into Argentina, the family boarded a Gulfstream G400 executive jet operated by Argentine airline Baires Fly. The aircraft flew to the United States, stopping to refuel in Guayaquil, Ecuador, before landing on Wednesday morning at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, CNN Brasil reported.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Recognising Hamas as 'terror' outfit: Eisenkot lays down conditions for 'broad Zionist government'
item.description:
Recognising Hamas as 'terror' outfit: Eisenkot lays down conditions for 'broad Zionist government'

Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has set out four conditions for forming a new government, including recognising Hamas as a "terrorist" organisation and committing to dismantle its military and governing capabilities in Gaza, as he seeks to use an opposition parliamentary majority to end Benjamin Netanyahu's rule.

In a statement posted on X on Saturday, the Yashar party leader said he was prepared to work with any elected lawmaker who accepted his principles for a broad "Zionist government".

These include recognising Israel as a "Jewish, democratic, liberal and egalitarian state", upholding the values of its Declaration of Independence, and introducing compulsory military or civilian national service for all citizens.

"The door to the government we will establish is open to every elected official who accepts these principles," he said, calling for an "extraordinary effort" to avoid another election and a prolonged political crisis.

Eisenkot vowed to move swiftly to use the new Knesset majority against what he called the "government of October 7", referring to the Netanyahu administration and its handling of the failures surrounding the Hamas-led attack on Israel in 2023.

He said a majority of Israeli voters, by more than half a million votes, had rejected the outgoing government and draft evasion in favour of political change. He pledged to introduce legislation establishing a state commission of enquiry into the 7 October failures, make national service compulsory for all Israelis and repeal the controversial judicial overhaul laws passed by the outgoing government.

The election, however, has produced a hung parliament, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. Anti-Netanyahu parties secured 67 seats, against 53 for the outgoing coalition, but the opposition total includes 48 seats held by Zionist parties and 19 won by the two Arab-led parties, the Joint List and Ra'am.

Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, while Eisenkot's Yashar finished second with 21. The opposition's numerical advantage therefore does not automatically translate into a governing majority, particularly given the reluctance of several Jewish opposition leaders to formally cooperate with Arab parties.

שבוע טוב. מספר דברים ממני אליכם, אחיי ואחיותיי הישראלים, לקראת הימים הקרובים: ספירת הקולות הסתיימה והבחירות נגמרו. בכל דרך בה מסתכלים על המספרים, רוב אזרחי ישראל, בהפרש של יותר מחצי מיליון קולות, הצביעו נגד ממשלת השבעה באוקטובר וההשתמטות, ובעד שינוי - רוב בקרב כלל אזרחי ישראל, ורוב בקרב הציבור הציוני המשרת. הגדרתי את הבחירות הללו בשנה האחרונה כגורליות ביותר בתולדות ישראל ותוצאותיהן ברורות, אף שיש מי שפועל להטיל בהן דופי. הבטחתי לחבר מחדש את ישראל ולשים סוף לתרבות השקר שהוביל נתניהו ופירקה אותנו מבפנים. הבטחתי שתחת הנהגתי, צד א׳ לא יכריע את צד ב׳, שתם עידן ״אנחנו״ ו״הם״. לאור הבטחות אלה אמשיך לפעול גם בשבועות הקרובים. במקביל, בכוונתי לפעול למימוש הרוב הפרלמנטרי המובהק באופן מיידי, לטובת כלל אזרחי ישראל. לפעול להקמת ועדת חקירה ממלכתית, קידום חובת שירות לכל ופעולה מיידית להגדלה וחיזוק היקף המשרתים בצה"ל, תגמול והוקרה ראויה למשרתים, ביטול חוקי ההפיכה המשטרית ועוד. אל תתנו לאף אחד להטעות אתכם: במדינת ישראל הכנסת היא שנותנת את אמונה בממשלה, ולא להפך. במהלך קמפיין הבחירות הצבתי מטרה להקים ממשלה ציונית ממלכתית עם הסכמה לאומית רחבה ככל האפשר שתביא לריפוי ושינוי יסודי בכיוון אליו ישראל הולכת. הצבתי באופן עקבי 4 עקרונות שיחזקו את ישראל, לכל שותפות: 1.⁠ ⁠הכרה בישראל כמדינה יהודית, דמוקרטית, ליברלית ושוויונית. 2.⁠ ⁠מחויבות לערכי מגילת העצמאות. 3.⁠ ⁠חובת שירות לכלל אזרחי ישראל - צבאי, לאומי ואזרחי. 4.⁠ ⁠הכרה בחמאס כארגון טרור ובחובה להשמדת הכוח הצבאי-שלטוני שלו ברצועת עזה. על בסיס עקרונות אלו, בכוונתי להקים ממשלה ציונית וממלכתית, רחבה ככל האפשר. לצורך כך אפעל בתיאום עם שותפיי ואפעל להרחיב את השותפות, על מנת לממש את רצון הבוחרים ולשפר באופן מיידי את מצבה הפנימי והבינלאומי של מדינת ישראל. כל חבר כנסת שמוכן לחתום על עקרונות אלו, הוא שותף אפשרי בדרך לכינון ממשלה חדשה וטובה לישראל. דלת הממשלה שנקים תהייה פתוחה לכל נבחר ציבור שמקבל את עקרונות אלו ונכון להתעלות לגודל השעה. ברור כי אחוזי ההצבעה הגבוהים, כמו גם האתגרים שעל הפרק, מחייבים מאמץ עילאי על מנת להימנע מבחירות נוספות וכניסה למשבר פוליטי מתמשך נוסף בכל דרך. ב-27.10 הציבור אמר את דברו וההחלטה על הרכבה של ממשלת ישראל הבאה היא של אזרחי ישראל בלבד, ללא מעורבות ומניפולציה - כך ראוי שיהיה. כעת מוטלת עלינו, נבחרי הציבור, החובה לעשות הכל על מנת לתרגם את רצון העם. מחדל השבעה באוקטובר ובהמשכו המציאות הביטחונית, הפנימית, הכלכלית והבינלאומית מחייבים החלטות אמיצות ובהקדם. אפעל בכל דרך להביא הסכמה לאומית רחבה ככל האפשר על מנת שנוכל להתחיל בתיקון ושיקום. לסיום, המלחמה נגד אויבינו לא תמה. מטרות המלחמה לא הושגו. עד להקמת הממשלה אתן גיבוי למהלכים צבאיים רק במידה ויהיו איומים ישירים ומיידיים כנגד ישראל שלא יכולים להמתין עד להשבעת הממשלה. לא נשלה את עצמנו. אנו בפני שבועות עמוסים, מורכבים ועתירי ספינים ושקרים. בכוונתי לפעול באומץ ומתוך מחויבות גדולה לבוחר ולמדינה על מנת לממש את רצונו - בשקט וביצירתיות. נעשה ונצליח, למען כולנו ולמען מדינת ישראל. אני מתחייב.

item.description:
Iran designates Britain's Royal Navy, RAF as 'terrorist' groups, report says

Iran's Foreign Ministry on Sunday designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist" organisations, in retaliation for what it described as hostile actions by the British government, including its designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a "terrorist organisation".

The ministry also designated Britain's foreign intelligence service, MI6, a "hostile group", saying the measures took effect on 1 November, according to Iran's Mehr News Agency.

The decision was taken under a resolution by Iran's Supreme National Security Council and followed Britain's designation of the IRGC under the State Threats Act 2026 on 13 July, the ministry said in a statement, Mehr reported.

Tehran also accused Britain of participating in the US-Israeli war against Iran by providing access to military and logistical bases and facilities under British jurisdiction.

The ministry said the measures were based on the principle of reciprocity and in accordance with international law, adding that the British government would be responsible for any consequences.

According to Mehr, the ministry condemned "Britain's anti-Iranian policies", saying they violated the principles of the United Nations Charter, including respect for national sovereignty and the prohibition of unlawful measures against other states.

Araghchi says Hormuz could be reopened within two days if conditions met

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said Hormuz could be reopened within two days if Washington agrees to a set of conditions, including the formal recognition of the new shipping route designated by Iran and Oman in the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi said other conditions include lifting the sanctions the US imposed on Iran after the collapse of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) in July; reducing the US military presence in the region; reinstating the oil waivers granted in June as part of the MoU; releasing frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar; formally recognising the new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz, set by Iran and Oman, and closing all other routes and ending the war on all fronts, particularly Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Araghchi told Al Jazeera that the plan currently under discussion is the one Iran originally presented at the beginning, known as the Iran seven-day plan, in which "we specified our condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz".

"Our Qatari friends asked to cut this time window from seven days to five days or less, and we worked on this idea during the Qatari delegation visit yesterday,” he said.

“We have now reached a plan that cuts the implementation time to two days. On day one, the US implements a set of measures. On day two, the Hormuz Strait will reopen, and navigation will be restored to what it used to be.”

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Asylum seekers still being sent to France under ‘one in one out’ weeks after scheme ended
item.description:
Guardian understands Home Office continues to detain dozens of people, with one group forcibly removed this week

The Home Office is still putting asylum seekers on to planes to France weeks after the controversial scheme to remove them ended, the Guardian has learned.

The “one in, one out” scheme was announced by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, and the former prime minister Keir Starmer in July 2025. It aimed to deter small boats crossing the Channel to the UK from northern France, with some asylum seekers arriving here forcibly returned to France while a similar number in northern France were brought legally to the UK.

She also argues that the money would be found in reducing the size of the civil service, and collapsing some government departments.
